title: Where to keep a signed-in session
subtitle: A signed cookie or a session kept on the server, side by side

scenes.title: Two ways to remember who is signed in
scenes.narration: A website can remember who you are in two ways. It can put everything in a signed cookie that your browser carries, or keep it on the server and give you only a ticket number.

rows.label: Size limit
cells: As much as the server allows

steps.say: With a signed cookie, the browser holds the whole session. With a server session, it holds only a random id.
Here is what each cookie looks like. One carries the user and their role, the other just a number.
The big difference is signing out. A stolen signed cookie keeps working until it expires. A server session can be deleted at once.
The cost is one extra read per request. In return there is no size limit.
Both are equally safe on the wire, as long as the cookie is marked secure.

scenes.kicker: Where to keep a signed-in session
scenes.narration: We picked the server session, because being able to sign someone out at once matters more than one fast read.
scenes.headline: Keep sessions **on the server**, and give the browser only a random id
items: Support can sign a user out of every device at once
Each request reads its session from Redis, about one millisecond
